slots.title: Beijing warns EU on curbs for Chinese firms
slots.body:

China’s Commerce Ministry framed the message as a response to Europe weighing “301”-style trade tools.

Talks this summer aim to shrink Europe’s record trade deficit with China; the calendar points to an October decision window.

slots.title: US close — Sept. 29, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,670.04, down 0.2% (13.65 points), after trading between 7,653.55 and 7,699.60.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.3% to 51,349.92; the Russell 2000 lost 0.4% to 2,807.92.

The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.1% to 26,797.54.

The VIX ended at 16.04, down 0.2% on the day.

At 14:00 ET the Conference Board reported September consumer confidence at 81.9, below the 89.2 estimate and down from 88.6 prior.

The same release window included JOLTs job openings for August at 7.079M vs 7.23M estimated (prior 7.335M), and job quits at 3.066M vs 3M estimated.

Utilities led Nasdaq sectors, up about 1.5% on average; financial services lagged, down about 1.0%.

Technology averaged about -0.6%; consumer cyclical about -0.6%; healthcare and industrials each up about 0.7%.

$META gained 3.2% to 738.79; $ASML gained 3.6% to 1,834.39; $TSM rose 0.9% to 456.94.

$AAPL fell 2.7% to 329.40; $TSLA lost 1.3% to 352.84; $WMT lost 1.8% to 106.80.

$CCL jumped 13.4% to 25.11 after EPS of 1.43 vs 1.35 estimated and revenue above estimate; $KMX rose 4.7% to 59.23 on a large EPS and revenue beat vs estimates.

$FICO closed down 26.5% at 617.87; $QURE down 37.3% at 24.51 among liquid decliners.

Gold futures rose 0.6% to 4,205.20; the US Oil Fund proxy ($USO) fell 4.4% to 143.35; Brent crude rose 0.4% to 96.53.

The dollar-bullish ETF proxy ($UUP) ticked up 0.2% to 28.75; bitcoin slipped 0.4% to 83,267.48.

Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.6% to 66,549.41; the FTSE 100 lost 0.5% and the Hang Seng edged down 0.1%.

Latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-09-25) showed the 10-year at 5.2% and the 2s10s spread at 0.36 percentage points.
